notes.174r.5: 'Whetstone-eye' renders the nickname slíkisteinsauga, 'sleekstone-eye'. Skrattavardi means 'warlock's cairn'.
notes.194r.17a: 194r.22a: the text reads seiðstaðr, 'sorcery place'; taken as seiðstafr, 'sorcery staff', since it was found with the bones.
notes.36.h: The last sentence ends in the next line with 'heil' ('well'): she was then with child.

Of Kotkel and Grima
This news travels
widely and is ill spoken of. Those were thought men not fit to live
who practised such sorcery
as Kotkel and his family had then shown. Heavily
did Gudrun take Thord's death, and she was not then
Thorleik home. And a little later they set out from home,
Kotkel and Grima and their sons. It was at night. They
went to Hrut's farm and worked a great *seiðr* [sorcery] there. And when
the sounds of the *seiðr* rose up, they did not feel they understood,
those who were inside, what it could mean. But lovely
was that chanting to hear. Hrut alone knew these
sounds, and told no one to look out that night,
and let each keep awake who can, and
then nothing will harm us, if it is handled so. But
everyone fell asleep all the same. Hrut stayed awake longest
and yet fell asleep. Kari was the name of a son of Hrut, who was then twelve
years old, and he was the most promising of the sons
of Hrut. He loved him greatly. Kari hardly slept
at all, because the game was aimed at him. He did not feel
very easy. Kari sprang up and looked out. He walked
into the *seiðr* and at once fell down dead. Hrut woke
in the morning, and his household, and
missed his son. He was found dead a short way
with fifteen men. And when Kotkel and his family see a party of men riding
to their farm, they make off into the mountain,
upwards. There Hallbjorn Whetstone-eye was
caught, and a bag was pulled over his head. At once
men were assigned to guard him, and some
went after Kotkel and Grima, up onto the mountain.
Kotkel and Grima were caught on the ridge
between Haukadal and Laxardal. They were
stoned to death there, and over them was made
a cairn of stones; its traces can be seen, and it is called Skrattavardi.
Stigandi got away south off the ridge
to Haukadal, and there he vanished from them. Hrut and
his sons went down to the sea with Hallbjorn. They launched
a boat and rowed out from land with him. Then they took
the bag off his head, and tied a stone to his neck.
Hallbjorn then turned his gaze on the land, and the look in his eyes
was not good. Then Hallbjorn said: It was no
lucky day either when we kinsmen came to Kambsnes
here to meet Thorleik. This I declare,
he says, that Thorleik shall have few days of pleasure there from now on,
and that all who settle in his place shall find it hard to live there.
This curse is thought to have come true to a great degree.
Then they drowned him and rowed to land. A little later
Hrut goes to see Olaf his kinsman, and tells

Then Herdis woke and told Gudrun the dream.
Gudrun thought the vision a good sign. The next morning
Gudrun had the boards taken up from the church floor where
she used to kneel in prayer. She had [men] dig there
down into the earth. Bones were found underneath. They were
dark and evil-looking. A brooch was also found there, and a *seiðr* [sorcery] staff,
a large one. People then thought they knew that there must
have been some seeress's grave. Those bones were
carried far away, to where people least often passed.
